title: candidate-ian-murphy-panel-debrief-scratchpad
content:
Quick panel debrief notes for Ian Murphy (runtime engineering candidate) — informal, raw. No decisions yet, saving thoughts for the hiring rubric and follow-up.

Context:
- Role: Senior/Principal (open to senior if comp/fit) — runtime inference team (KV cache, batching, latency SLOs).
- Loop: 3 interviews today (system design, kernel/latency optimizations, behavioral/culture). Panel: Marcus (system design), Danielle (serving runtime internals), Samir (team fit & shipping). I moderated intro + salary/expectations.
- Candidate background: 6.5 years infra+ML infra; past at a medium ML infra startup (edge serving) + earlier infra at FAANG. Strong experience with latency-focused systems, some CUDA exposure but more focused on C++ runtime and RPCs.

High-level impression (TL;DR):
- Strengths: pragmatic latency tradeoffs, clear mental models for KV cache and prefix caching; good at decomposing tail-latency problems; solid ownership examples.
- Concerns: less hands-on with GPU kernels/quantization internals than we expected for Principal; some gaps on multi-tenant isolation strategies at infra scale (autoscaling preemption behavior).
- Recommendation at the moment: strong "yes" for Senior role; lean "maybe" for Principal unless follow-up shows deeper low-level GPU/quantization exposure.

Scorecard (rough):
- System design: 4/5 (well structured, considered SLOs, sensible fallback designs)
- Latency/Perf internals: 3.5/5 (great at caching/batching heuristics, weaker on GPU kernel-level tradeoffs)
- Ownership & shipping: 5/5 (clear examples of driving features to production and measuring regressions)
- Culture/communication: 4.5/5 (concise communicator, good cross-team examples)
- Overall fit: 4/5 (good hire at Senior, borderline at Principal)

Notes by interviewer:
- Marcus (system design): liked the choice of metrics-first approach (P50/P95/P99 + p99.9 traces). Proposed canary rollout + automatic fallback to smaller model variant on overload — practical. Asked about routing policy complexity and Ian suggested a lightweight policy engine (rule-based + metrics). He worried about rule proliferation; suggested tiered policies.
- Danielle (runtime internals): Ian explained KV cache eviction policy (LRU + size aware segmenting) and batch formation heuristics (time-window + priority). Good mental model for memory pressure and observed throughput. When pushed on GPU memory fragmentation and kernel fusion tradeoffs, he was candid: limited exposure to writing CUDA kernels, more experienced in staging/pre-processing & runtime orchestration.
- Samir (team & leadership): strong on owning on-call incidents — described a 48-hour tie-out where they traced a tail-latency regression to a stray GC interaction in a dependency and rolled a compatibility shim. Advocated for postmortems and dedicated regression test harnesses.

Behavioral / Red flags:
- No glaring red flags. Candidate asked good clarifying questions about our rollout cadence and SLA expectations.
- Minor hesitation: when asked about multi-tenant noisy-neighbor mitigation at 100s of GPUs scale, proposed sensible mitigations (quota shaping, backpressure) but lacked examples of operating at that scale. Could be because prior role ran smaller fleets.

Open questions / follow-ups we should get answers to before finalizing level:
- Concrete examples of GPU-interfacing work: any PRs/repos where Ian contributed kernel-level changes or quantization-aware inference pieces? (Ask for links.)
- Depth on multi-tenant isolation at scale: were they involved in capacity planning / autoscaler nuance for preemptible instances? specific incident examples?
- Preference on IC vs manager track; comp expectations (range given briefly but want firm numbers).

Suggested next steps:
1) Ask Ian for 2–3 repos/PRs that show lower-level work (if available). If none, that's fine — treat as Senior-level hire.
2) If team wants to push for Principal, schedule a 30–45m follow-up with an applied ML infra engineer who owns quantization/kernel work (to probe depth).
3) Draft a concise feedback blurb for hiring committee (I can draft). Include recommended level and compensation band.

Draft feedback blurb (for reuse in forms):
"Ian Murphy demonstrated strong systems thinking and ownership around latency-sensitive serving systems. He shows excellent judgment for caching, batching, and rollout strategies and has firsthand experience debugging complex regressions in production. He has less hands-on experience with low-level GPU kernels and quantization internals; recommend hiring at Senior level where his ownership and orchestration skills will be high-impact. Consider Principal only if follow-up shows additional kernel/quantization depth."

Personal notes / heuristics:
- Would accelerate onboarding on our infra (observability + rollout tools) given his incident experience.
- Good candidate for projects like intelligent routing policies, KV caching improvements, or autoscaler robustness work.
- Not the immediate pick if we need someone to implement custom CUDA kernels this quarter.

Misc (notes-to-self):
- Save this to candidate folder and link to JIRA-8675.
- Remind hiring panel to fill rubric by EOD Friday.
- Follow up with Ian on repos + firm comp by Monday.

End of scratchpad.
